text:
sara_support: FYI customer reported a big latency delta — calls from their private VPC keep landing in eu-west instead of our us-west edge. They say this started after a firewall/NAT change on their appliance.

miguel_oncall: can you paste a sample request id + timestamps? also any traceroute/tcpdump they ran?

sara_support: sample X-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c3d, first seen 2147499000. Customer ran traceroute from their onprem gateway and shows a hops list into our eu-edge loadbalancer IP. They also confirmed we see the incoming SNATed IP from their gateway rather than the original VM IP.

elaine_networks: quick hypothesis — our edge selection does a 5-tuple hash (src ip, src port, dst ip, dst port, proto) to pick region pool. If their gateway SNATs to a small rotating ephemeral IP/port range that hashes to eu, all traffic could stick there.

raj_infra: can you ask them for a tcpdump of the egress at their gateway? capture should show original src and post-snat mapping. also ask them to run: 

```
sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 203.0.113.45 and port 443 -w snat-capture.pcap
traceroute -n 34.210.12.9 # our us-west front IP
traceroute -n 52.16.33.5 # our eu-west front IP
```

sara_support: sending repro steps to customer now. they replied with pcap and both traceroutes. pcap shows gateway SNAT to 198.51.100.22 and source ports are in the 40000-40010 range. traceroute to our us-west IP times out mid-aspath; traceroute to eu-west completes.

miguel_oncall: that port range is tiny — consistent hash will likely map that combination to eu pool. ask them if they just enabled port-preserving SNAT or a small pool.

elaine_networks: also check if their peering side is advertising a more specific route to eu egress by accident. but pcap + small port range is highly suspicious.

raj_infra: short-term mitigation options:
- request them to expand SNAT port range (high ephemeral range) or enable true 1:1 NAT so src IP varies
- we can add a routing override for that customer’s SNATed IP to prefer us-west (workaround)
- or we add a check to our region routing to prefer origin ASN/peered-cidr mapping before 5-tuple hash for peered traffic

autoscale-bot: Created ticket SPT-1234: "onprem SNAT port-range causes source-hash -> eu pool" assigned to eng-infra, priority P2.

sara_support: customer can expand SNAT range tomorrow morning; they want us to test meanwhile. can someone run a quick live test mapping: simulate SNATed ip 198.51.100.22 and ports 40000..40010 and confirm which edge pool that hashes to?

raj_infra: running small script now from our side to hash-map: 
```
# pseudo: compute 5-tuple consistent-hash for dst=our-front-usw, proto=6(tcp)
# src ips: 198.51.100.22, ports: 40000-40010
```
result: all ports map to eu-west pool (confirmed).

miguel_oncall: ok that matches customer's symptom. next steps: 1) ask customer to broaden ephemeral ports or use 1:1 NAT, 2) we push a temporary routing override for 198.51.100.22 to west pool (low risk, timeboxed), 3) longer term: change route selection heuristic for peered SNATs.

elaine_networks: I can push the routing override after change window, but need customer's written approval. sara, can you get that?

sara_support: will request approval and confirm schedule. also collected pcap + traceroutes and attached to SPT-1234.

raj_infra: logging note: add this SNATed IP to our monitoring alert so if it flips pools again we get paged.

miguel_oncall: thanks team. marking follow-up for eng-infra to evaluate adding peered-cidr precedence in routing code.

sara_support: customer acknowledged and will expand port range tomorrow. keeping SPT-1234 open until we see traffic shift back to us-west. :thumbsup:
